subject: maths
title: Dot Product Domain
description: Use a·b = |a||b|cosθ to find angles and check perpendicularity.

concepts.def: a·b = a₁b₁ + a₂b₂ + a₃b₃ — a scalar (number).
a·b = |a||b|cosθ where θ is the angle between vectors.
If a·b = 0 and neither is zero, the vectors are perpendicular.
a parallel to b means a = kb for some scalar k.

options: Perpendicular
Parallel
Equal
Zero

mcqs.q: If the dot product of two non-zero vectors is zero, what does that mean?
options: It means at least one of the vectors is the zero vector.
The vectors are perpendicular to each other.
It means the vectors are parallel.
The magnitude is 12 — you multiply the components.

mcqs.q: What is the magnitude of the vector (3, 4)?
options: The magnitude is 12 — you multiply the components.
5 — using sqrt(3^2 + 4^2).
The magnitude is 7 — you add the components.
(-3)^2 equals -6 because the negative makes you subtract.
It means the vectors are parallel.
(-3)^2 equals -6 because the negative makes you subtract.
(-3)^2 equals -9 because the minus is preserved.
9 — squaring a negative gives a positive.
